text:
noah: Hey all 

Just finished onboarding and trying to standardize my devtoolchain on an M2. Using asdf for node/python/rust (asdf-rust plugin), Homebrew at /opt/homebrew, and want to keep go via brew. I hit three things: 1) cargo build failing because openssl not found, 2) go tooling installed into /usr/local/go not on PATH, 3) my devcontainer uses bash but I prefer fish so envs mismatch. Any compact tips?  

anya: Welcome! :wave: Quick checklist that helped me:  
- Keep a single package manager for system libs (Homebrew /opt/homebrew).  
- For rust/cargo openssl issues: `brew install openssl@3 pkg-config` and then `export OPENSSL_DIR=/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3` before `cargo build`.  
- For asdf plugins that build native code, set LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS/PKG_CONFIG_PATH to point at brew libs. Example:  
```bash
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/zlib/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig"
asdf install rust latest
```  

matt: For Go, avoid the brew default that installs to /usr/local on Intel. Use `brew install go` (arm) or set GOPATH and add `$(brew --prefix)/opt/go/libexec/bin` to PATH. Also ensure `go env GOMODCACHE` points where you expect.  

clair: On devcontainers: if your container image uses bash, but your dotfiles set fish, add a shell init hook in the container's Dockerfile or use `SHELL: /usr/bin/fish` in devcontainer.json. Alternatively, put universal env bits (PATH + PKG_CONFIG_PATH) in a file sourced by both shells, e.g., `~/.profile` or `/etc/profile.d/redwood-dev.sh`.  

noah: Re: cargo, I did brew install openssl@3 and export OPENSSL_DIR but build still errors with "failed to find openssl headers". Any debug commands?  

anya: Run `pkg-config --cflags openssl` and `pkg-config --libs openssl` to see what paths are being used. If pkg-config prints nothing, your PKG_CONFIG_PATH is wrong. Also check `rustup show` to confirm toolchain and `rustc -vV`.  

matt: Another cause: cargo build inside an editor terminal launched by GUI may not see your shell init. Always `exec $SHELL` or reopen the terminal after changing dotfiles. For VSCode specifically, use "remote.containers.postStartCommand": "source /etc/profile.d/redwood-dev.sh || true" in devcontainer.json.  

clair: If you plan to keep fish as primary, add shared env file and source it from fish, bash, zsh, e.g. in fish: `source ~/.profile; set -x PATH $PATH` so both interactive shells get same PATH.  

noah: Thanks 

One last: I installed some old global npm packages with sudo earlier and now permission errors pop up when npm tries to write to /usr/local. Best fix?  

matt: Don't use sudo for npm. Fix perms: `sudo chown -R $(whoami) $(npm root -g) $(npm cache dir)` or reinstall node via asdf (which uses local shims) so global packages live in your HOME.  

dotfiles-bot: Please add any Mac-specific notes to the dotfiles repo under macos/multi-language.md and include the template changelog entry.  

noah: Will do, opening a tiny PR with the OPENSSL_DIR and shared-profile snippet. Thanks all!
